# Noise budget

Calculated from the specification before the front end was simulated and
before the behavioural converter existed. Each contributor has its own
closed form transfer function in
[model/daqmodel/noise_budget.py](../../model/daqmodel/noise_budget.py); none
of it uses a circuit solver. The ngspice deck generated from the same
netlist is the independent check (`scripts/run_ngspice.py`, results in
[test-results/noise-floor/ngspice_crosscheck.csv](../../test-results/noise-floor/ngspice_crosscheck.csv)).

## Method

* Temperature 27 degC, the ngspice default, so both routes use the same
  4kT.
* Output referred power spectral density at the converter pins is summed
  over contributors, weighted by the sinc4 decimator's |H(f)|^2 and
  integrated. The decimator response is periodic in f_mod, so the integral
  runs to 2.458 MHz and counts the analogue noise that folds back
  from around the modulator clock. The converter's own noise is defined in
  band and is integrated to f_mod / 2 only.
* Equivalent noise bandwidth of the decimator at 2400 SPS:
  **575.24 Hz**.
* Input referred figures divide by the DC gain of the gain setting.
* Modulator quantisation noise uses the linear model (white error of
  variance 1/3 shaped by the NTF). A 1-bit loop is not linear, so this is a
  conservative estimate; the behavioural model measures the real figure.

## Allowances

The amplifier, converter and reference figures are allowances: what the
budget permits each part to contribute. They are not quoted from a
datasheet and part selection has to meet them.

| Part | Allowance |
|---|---|
| Gain stage amplifiers (zero drift, so no 1/f term) | e_n 6 nV/rtHz, i_n 0.3 pA/rtHz, each |
| Converter, referred to its input | 20 nV/rtHz |
| Reference after its RC filter | 20 nV/rtHz |

## What the budget says about the design

* At gain 1 the converter's own noise and the modulator quantisation
  dominate, followed by the two feedback resistors. A unity gain buffer
  without R_f would be quieter but the resistors stay because the gain is
  switched by R_G alone.
* From gain 8 up the gain stage amplifiers' voltage noise dominates
  (63 percent of the power at gain 8,
  76 percent at gain 128) and the protection
  resistors are most of the rest, so the noise stops falling with gain.
  Lowering it further means a quieter amplifier or less protection
  resistance, not more gain.
* Amplifier current noise is negligible with this source impedance; it
  would matter only above about 20 kohm per leg.
* Analogue alias rejection at f_mod - 500 Hz is
  **66.9 dB** from the two RC poles
  (11.24 kHz and 15.19 kHz), against a target of
  60 dB.
* Predicted SNR for a -1 dBFS sine at gain 1, reference noise included:
  **126.9 dB**, an ENOB of 20.79 bits before distortion.
